_readme: Medical DAPT / DoRA ablation -- ALL knobs for the Qwen3.5-4B-Base run.
Logic lives in dapt_lib.py, the run itself in steps/*.py (one file per notebook
cell), narrative in the notebook. This file is data only: edit it, re-run the
notebook's preamble cell (it git-pulls) and then step 04.
WHY JSON HAS NO COMMENTS: every non-obvious knob carries a sibling '_why' string
right next to it. Keep them when you fork a variant -- they are the provenance.
VARIANTS: a one-off experiment does not have to touch this file. Add
configs/<name>.json with only the keys you change, pass its name as `OVERRIDES`
in the notebook preamble, and dapt_lib deep-merges it over this file.
See configs/ctx4096.json for a worked example.
THE ONE RULE: budget.sec_per_step is a PLACEHOLDER (12.0) until you run probe().
A wrong s/step does not error -- it silently rescales tokens/arm, which is the
only thing that makes arms comparable.
budget.seq_len is the REFERENCE length the token budget is defined at
(tokens/arm = steps x effective_batch x seq_len). To change context, set an
ARM's max_length -- never seq_len, which would silently rescale tokens/arm.
An arm at a longer context gets proportionally fewer steps for the same tokens.
_model_why: Was Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B. Same arch family (qwen3_5, hybrid 3 linear : 1 full attn, vocab 248320) so the adapter/tokenizer surface is unchanged. 4.66B total = 4.35B text + 0.31B ViT. Needs transformers >= 5.2.0. This base TIES word embeddings (the 27B does not) -- cell 8 / build_model() asserts on that.

budget._wall_h_why: The knob to think in. 1.0 h/arm = 192 steps, and the fixed 0.36 h per-arm overhead is 36% of that clock. 3.0 h = 792 steps / 26.0M tokens. 5.0 h = 1392 steps / 45.6M tokens. 6 arms x 5.0 h = 30 h.
budget._total_why: Ceiling for the whole grid: 30 h grid + 10 h for the two B seed reps + 5 h margin. The driver stops before exceeding it.
budget._sec_per_step_why: PLACEHOLDER for the 4B on the RTX 6000 Pro (G4), scaled from the measured 27B number (36.0) by the 4.35B-vs-27B text-param ratio. RUN probe() FIRST. ~12 s/step = 2731 tok/s = 9.83M tok/h.
budget._text_params_why: Text tower only, used for the tok/param readout. The ViT adds ~0.31B and never trains here.

overheads._eval_per_source_why: Held-out rows per source. 200 was 2x this; the eval cost is counted in the budget so it cannot drift.
overheads._evals_per_run_why: Eval points DURING training. The overhead term adds step-0 and final on top, so it is (2 + evals_per_run) full passes.

trainer._warmup_why: The DAPT recipe uses 6% of steps.
trainer._eval_batch_why: HF default 8 would blow VRAM in eval.
trainer._best_model_why: load_best_model_at_end is meaningless over a couple of hundred steps, so it only switches on for saves AND steps >= this.

saving._save_why: Screen pass: NO. The screen's product is the LOSS NUMBERS, not weights. modules_to_save writes the FULL embed_tokens + lm_head, and on this base the pair stays TIED (PEFT points lm_head at the embedding's copy), so a checkpoint writes it once: ~1.4 GB, not the ~2.5 GB two independent copies would cost. Set true -- or list ids in save_arms -- for the confirm stage and for ANY run that outlives one session: without a checkpoint there is nothing to resume from and the run is lost.

lora._mts_why: embed/head can only be trained through modules_to_save on this path: finetune_vision_layers=False enables scoping and the finetune_* filter silently drops them from target_modules. On a TIED base never wrap only one of the pair. An arm that sets modules_to_save=null (ADONLY) freezes both and trains the adapter only -- build_model() asserts the tie is intact in that case.
lora._rslora_why: rsLoRA conflicts with DoRA; left here as an explicit false so a variant cannot quietly switch it on.

data._mix_why: 72% medical, 28% general. The general slice is the FORGETTING GUARD: it is the only thing that can catch a medical run that destroyed general ability. Sum must be 1.0 (asserted).
data._checkpoint_metric_why: With a dict eval_dataset there is NO plain eval_loss -- HF prefixes every key with the dataset name, so exactly one dataset must be named here.

baseline._rank_why: alpha = 2*r keeps the effective scaling alpha/r = 2 identical to the original r=128 config, and r=32 is 1.25% of the base instead of 4.93%. Every arm's adapter is <= 1.25% here; the DoRA paper's own LLaMA-7B setup is 2.31%/2.33%.
baseline._emblr_why: embedding_learning_rate = learning_rate * this = 1e-5. Decoupled because the embed/head pair is 0.636B of the 0.694B trainable parameters (91.6% of everything that moves) -- and on this stack the pair is TIED, so it counts once, not twice (see _tying_why). ARM EMB1 sets it to 1.0 to test whether the decoupling is needed at all.
baseline._tying_why: MEASURED on this stack (Qwen3.5-4B-Base, tie_word_embeddings=True, unsloth 2026.10.3 + transformers 5.17.0 + peft): the tie is KEPT whether this is false or true. With modules_to_save=['embed_tokens','lm_head'] PEFT wrapped BOTH, moved lm_head out of modules_to_save into modules_to_tie (peft#2777) and pointed it at the SAME trainable tensor as the embedding's copy -- one tensor, 0.636B params, and the head cannot drift from the embedding. So this knob is a NO-OP here, not a lever and not a grid arm; the param and checkpoint numbers in this file come from build_model()'s live count, never from a plan. It would matter again only on a stack where the default really does deep-copy both, so build_model() reports which of the two states actually happened either way.

_grid_why: Cut from 10 arms. Removed: r=128 (4.93% of the base) and r=256 (9.83%) entirely -- both are over the ~1-2% adapter line with a known answer, since rank saturates at 8-32; r=64 (2.47%) for the same reason; LR 3e-5 (redundant direction when 1e-4 -> 3e-4 brackets the ~2e-4 default in one arm); lora_dropout 0.05 (not a lever at this token budget); max_length 4096 (a deployment choice, and for the same tokens it would cost half the steps).

ADONLY is the one arm that is NOT a one-factor tweak: it changes what is trainable. It exists because modules_to_save makes the embed/head pair 0.636B of the 0.694B trainable parameters (on this stack the pair is tied, so it counts once). Freezing it takes trainable from 0.694B to 58.1M (11.9x), grads + 8-bit optimizer state from ~2.8 GB to ~0.23 GB, checkpoints from ~1.4 GB to ~0.12 GB, and lifts data exposure from 0.066 to 0.785 tokens per trainable parameter. Read it as its own recipe, not as a delta from B.

ruler._tol_why: Allowed rise in a guard (general-ability) loss before the arm is VETOED regardless of how good its domain loss is. Each arm is compared against its OWN step-0 baseline.

probe._warmup_why: The Mamba/GDN Triton kernels compile at load, so the first few steps are not representative. Discarded before timing.

phase0._phase0_why: The grid answers 'which config ranks best'; it cannot answer 'did the medical mix move this base', because 45M tokens is 0.010 tokens/param and canonical DAPT is 1-7. This curve runs ONLY the baseline at growing step counts: 300 -> 8000 steps spans 9.8M -> 262M tokens (0.002 -> 0.060 tok/param) and ~1.4 -> 27 h. The bend is the answer, and it also tells you which grid budget is worth spending. Runs >= force_save_min_steps checkpoint and can resume. Cheaper alternative: the same curve on Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base -- same family and tokenizer, ~5.4x the tokens/param for the same wall clock, and the recipe ranking transfers.

env._tf_why: Below 5.2 the qwen3_5 arch does not exist; 5.19.0 is on PyPI and is outside Unsloth's tested range (ceiling 5.17.0). datasets < 5.0.0 and trl <= 1.13.0 for the same reason. bf16 is mandatory: the GDN layers give NaN grad norms in fp16. Do not switch to QLoRA -- unsloth advises against 4-bit for Qwen3.5.
